tiers.core: Pinned by the kit as a git submodule under .claude/skills/ext/ and installed by default.
tiers.extension: Pinned by the kit the same way and installed on demand: bash .claude/bin/skills.sh add <id>. An entry with a skills list is not a submodule: skills.sh fetches those folders from its source into .claude/skills/<name>/.
tiers.add-on: Entries without a tier are opt-in tools the kit does not pin. Install one only when the user asks.

commit: Every core and extension entry records the commit it is pinned at: for a submodule, the gitlink validate.sh checks the entry against; for a skills-list pack, the commit skills.sh fetches and asserts against FETCH_HEAD. bash .claude/bin/skills.sh pins rechecks them, --write rewrites them from the gitlinks.
triggers: Display text: the INSTALL WHEN column of skills.sh list, for people and agents choosing a pack. Nothing matches on it.
scope: Skill packs, plugins, template repos and catalogs — things an installer can put on disk. MCP servers are not listed here and never were installable from here: skills.sh writes no .mcp.json and runs no claude mcp add. A default server lives in .mcp.json; an opt-in one is a line in .claude/commands/setup-mcp.md that the user runs.

entries.name: Solana Fuzz Skill
entries.description: The Trident harness API at a pinned version, plus the flag that makes a fuzz run mean anything. Two things the kit does not already have: the v0.12.0 call surface written out (#[flow_executor], #[init]/#[flow]/#[end], process_transaction, get_account_with_type and its discriminator offset, PDA seeds in fuzz_accounts) so an agent stops authoring Trident calls from memory against an API that moves every minor version; and the --with-exit-code trap, where a failing invariant is swallowed in parallel mode and the run still exits 0, so a green CI job proves nothing. No other pinned pack mentions that flag, and /test-rust and /audit-solana both print trident fuzz run without it. It layers under auditor-skill rather than overlapping: that pack already calls Trident the default primary harness and ships 19 invariants phrased as Trident post-conditions, deciding what to assert; this one is how to build the harness that asserts it. Ships one runnable Anchor example that goes red on a planted wrapping_sub bug and green on the fix, pins Trident 0.12.0 stable over the 0.13 RC, and marks its own regression and trident compare surface as unverified.
entries.safety: clean; no env keys, no nested submodules, and it only writes test code. The Trident CLI it drives is a separate cargo install trident-cli --locked, and a fuzz run builds and executes the program under test, so run it on code you intend to build. Pinned pre-fix: the worked example still pins anchor-lang 0.31 and uses the pre-1.0 space = 8 + INIT_SPACE form (belumume/solana-fuzz#1, fix open in #2). That is the example program only -- the harness API this pack is pinned for is unaffected, since trident-tests/ depends on borsh and trident-fuzz and not on anchor-lang.

entries.name: Sign-Safe
entries.description: Signing-time safety gate: decodes an opaque base64 transaction or message (legacy and v0 with Address Lookup Tables), classifies instructions against a danger-primitive catalog, screens recipients against a drainer blocklist, and emits a SIGN / HOLD / REJECT verdict plus a machine-readable verdict.json for gating an agent's signing. Offline and deterministic by default. Complements auditor-skill: that audits the program, this one reviews the transaction about to be signed.
triggers: is this transaction safe to sign
entries.safety: clean at this pin: no eval, atob, createRequire or new Function anywhere; no network in the deterministic core, and its own tests assert no http/axios/undici import leaks into it; spawnSync and execFileSync appear only in test harnesses, with shell false and static argument arrays; no install lifecycle hooks. Egress only through an --rpc endpoint you pass yourself. About 5.8 MB checked out, 93% of it a dev-only mainnet transaction corpus the runtime never reads (upstream issue 29)

entries.name: Solana Counterparty Gate
entries.description: Operator-reputation gate for a program, oracle, keeper or multisig you did not write: asks whether the deployer behind it is a known serial rug operator before you CPI into it or compose with it. Answers the question a bytecode audit cannot. Backed by SolSentry's hosted mainnet scanner, so its verdicts are only as current as that service.
triggers: is this deployer a rug operator
entries.safety: clean at this pin: no eval, atob, createRequire or code-execution primitives; the only network caller is tests/smoke.sh via curl. Caution on data flow rather than code: it queries SolSentry's hosted API at api.solsentry.app (read endpoints need no key; override with SOLSENTRY_API_URL), so the counterparty addresses you ask about go to a third party, and an outage degrades it to no answer rather than a wrong one. Smallest pack the kit pins, about 144 KB checked out

entries.name: Solana Airdrop (Merkle distribution)
entries.description: Merkle-tree airdrops: recipient ingestion, root and per-recipient proofs, claim-instruction building for the Solana Foundation template and Metaplex gumdrop, anti-double-claim PDA derivation, anti-sybil eligibility patterns. A zero-dependency pure-Python Keccak-256 engine plus a TypeScript claim builder.

install.command: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yusizer/solana-airdrop-skill && cd solana-airdrop-skill && bash install.sh .

entries.safety: no malware: scanned at 1b708843cd8104e3dd4433a0e85a6b443ed4c711 — no eval, atob or createRequire, no network egress, no keypair reads, stdlib-only Python. Its Keccak-256 is correct (cross-checked against SHA3 over 305 input lengths). Correctness caveats, though, and they matter because airdrop roots are irreversible: verify_all() is self-referential and cannot fail, so it does not catch a wrong leaf encoding, and its eval grades itself against its own root. De-dup keys on (pubkey, amount) while the Foundation template's claim PDA is per-claimant, so a repeated pubkey strands funds. The claim builder asks for a Keypair where a PublicKey would do, and its install.sh overwrites a project's agents, commands and rules without asking. See upstream issue 1; treat its gate as a self-consistency check and verify a root against the target program's own tooling before publishing
